init: Block symlinks and FIFOs on the stateful file system. This makes use of the inode security policy code added to the chromiumos LSM in the kernel. By default, symlink traversal and opening of FIFOs on the stateful file system are now blocked. There are exceptions to the symlink policy for a handful of file system locations that actually do rely on symlinks. gcc: Update wrapper for non-hardened toolchain. The current wrapper for non-hardened toolchain could not handle clang. Make it work by migrating to the hardened wrapper with these changes: 1. Split the current hardening wrapper info flags/body. 2. Hardened non-hardened toolchains have their own set of gcc/clang/common flags. This also brings these new features to the unhardened toolchain: 1. Ability to bisect object files. 2. clang syntax checking (if enabled via -clang-syntax) Note: llvm host wrapper is not affected since it does not use any of the modified files. There is minimal difference between the final generated wrapper for hardened toolchain. BUg=chromium:819464 TEST=sudo emerge cross-arm-none-eabi/gcc works. TEST=sudo emerge cross-armv7m-cros-eabi/compiler-rt works. TEST=sudo emerge cross-armv7a-cros-linux-gnueabihf/gcc works. midis: Don't create devices which have no MIDI ports. There is a bug where devices are created if they have a non-zero number of subdevices, even if none of those are MIDI. This patch makes the creation of a device contingent on how many *MIDI Ports* the device is reporting to ALSA. This patch also fixes a bug, where we weren't returning when Device::WriteClientDataToDevice() received a call to write to a non-existent port (the first fix should now make this impossible, but we should add the return just in case, to prevent a segfault). BUG=chromium:820336 TEST=unit tests, used djay app with Mixon 4 device. Change-Id: Ibc4ad07447b34a90101c31cc6c150f6166921fde Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/956886 Commit-Ready: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Tested-by: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: FROMGIT: drm/amdgpu: set DRIVER_ATOMIC flag early The atomic debugfs stuff gets created in drm_dev_alloc() but this gets called before we've enumerated all of our IPs, so move the DRIVER_ATOMIC flag setting to fix that. Since DRIVER_ATOMIC is a driver flag it's currently global to the driver so setting it affects all GPUs driven by the driver. Unfortunately, not all GPUs support atomic. Warn the user if that is the case. This is the same as our current behavior, but at least the atomic debugfs stuff gets created now. Backport: trivial conflicts in both amdgpu_drv.c and amdgpu_dm.c BUG=none TEST=/sys/kernel/debug/dri/0/state exists Acked-by: Harry Wentland <harry.wentland@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit 3fa203af4bd0c7eb09f21af34d3a68e08583feac git://people.freedesktop.org/~agd5f/linux branch:amd-staging-drm-next) Signed-off-by: Drew Davenport <ddavenport@chromium.org> Change-ID: I32ea4880713bbbfa217d95364b513d2189d1bc0d Change-Id: I32ea4880713bbbfa217d95364b513d2189d1bc0d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/891681 Commit-Ready: Drew Davenport <ddavenport@chromium.org> Tested-by: Drew Davenport <ddavenport@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kristian H.
